cohort: The study included 252 singleton pregnancies, comprising 84 conceived via IVF (fresh or frozen-thawed embryo transfer) and 168 via natural conception, at a single university hospital.
finding: The study found that placental volume was significantly greater in the FET group, fresh embryo transfer newborns were significantly smaller than controls and FET newborns, and postpartum haemorrhage was far more frequent in FET pregnancies.
